name: Hatebreed
label: Victory
lede: A prep cook's weekend band got thrown off Warped Tour, found a home in metal, and watched its singer take over the host's chair on MTV2's Headbangers Ball.

eras.title: Prep cook by day, breakdowns by weekend
eras.text: Hatebreed came out of the New Haven and West Haven hardcore scene, built around a teenage Jamey Jasta who had been booking shows at The Moon. Three of the five founders were gone by the end of 1996, and the version that cut Satisfaction Is the Death of Desire gave Victory Records its best-selling debut.

years.src: Louder (Metal Hammer): Jamey Jasta, My Life Story · Wikipedia: Jamey Jasta
years.h: A 16-year-old Jamey Jasta borrows his grandfather's car to start Hatebreed
years.p: The line-up: Chris Beattie on bass, Wayne Lozinak and Larry Dwyer Jr. on guitars, Dave Russo on drums. The template was [[Madball|c9e0a0f5-9f53-4247-a52d-a3f29d975e17]], [[Entombed|61b99cc4-06cd-4ad5-9bac-950b2daef9cc]] and [[Earth Crisis|88a6037e-87ba-492a-a54c-c927aa620cb8]].
years.xp:
Jasta had been going to every kind of show at The Moon in New Haven since he was 12 or 13. His first band, Dreadnaught (later Jasta 14), opened for [[Sick of It All|e204ed91-3684-4561-b29b-d0b53f8459a7]].

He told Metal Hammer he worked as a prep cook during the week while Hatebreed practiced and played Thursday to Sunday.

years.h: Under the Knife costs $150 and the band's own money
years.p: After a 1995 demo and a split 7" with Neglect, Hatebreed's first EP stalled at Big Wheel Recreation, so the band put it out itself.
years.xp: Jamey Jasta told Metal Hammer the recording cost $150, all of it out of the band's pockets.

years.h: Out go three founders, in comes Lou "Boulder" Richards
years.p: Wayne Lozinak, Larry Dwyer Jr. and Dave Russo are gone by the end of 1996. Nick Papantoniou takes the drums for 1996-97 and Lou Richards joins on guitar.

years.h: Chris Bickel of In/Humanity says Hatebreed surrounded him at a show
years.p: Per Wikipedia, Bickel criticized Victory Records in his zine, then was surrounded at a Hatebreed show by band members who threatened him with homophobic slurs.
years.xp:
Wikipedia reports that Jamey Jasta later left Bickel a threatening voicemail calling himself a homophobe. In/Humanity played the voicemail at their own shows, and Hatebreed answered with hostile stage banter when they played In/Humanity's hometown of Columbia, South Carolina.

No response from Hatebreed to the account appears in the sources checked.

years.src: Wikipedia: Satisfaction Is the Death of Desire · Louder (Metal Hammer)
years.h: Victory signs Hatebreed, and the sellout talk starts
years.p: Satisfaction Is the Death of Desire was produced by [[Steve Evetts|ae091a4c-0a25-4555-8874-5f05768d9d18]], with Matt McIntosh and Lou Richards on guitars and Jamie Pushbutton of [[Death Threat|10bc16b4-567d-4bb0-b455-3ad0db178975]] on drums. SoundScan counted 158,000 copies, Victory's best-selling debut.
years.xp:
Critics called the label the McDonald's of hardcore. Jamey Jasta told Metal Hammer he was heartbroken, and pointed out that [[Strife|5e911223-4228-4a14-8f6c-7d2dfeb62530]] and [[Integrity|f626335d-d234-408d-a67c-37a3c2c7e98a]] were on Victory too.

The album is what got Hatebreed its Universal deal. Kerrang!, Loudwire and Revolver have all since ranked it among the most important metalcore records ever made.

eras.title: Kicked off Warped, adopted by metal
eras.text: Hatebreed's reputation was chaos: drunk, broke, and banned from the biggest punk tour in America. The metal world took the band in instead, and a major label bet on a record Jasta built to be as hard as possible.

years.big: "Being thrown off Warped Tour was our push into the metal world"
q: It was a learning experience and it helped us be less drunk and more professional.
yt: Hatebreed live at the Fireside Bowl, Chicago, Feb 1998
years.h: Kevin Lyman bans Hatebreed from Warped Tour
years.p: Hatebreed was kicked off Warped Tour 1998 for being drunk and disorderly, and stayed banned until 2017.
years.xp:
Jasta told Kerrang! the ban sent Hatebreed to Tattoo the Earth in 2000 and Ozzfest in 2001, the start of four Ozzfest summers.

He and founder Kevin Lyman eventually became friends again. Hatebreed played Lyman's Mayhem Festival in 2010 and 2011, then returned to Warped Tour in 2017.

years.h: Anal Cunt's crowd gets Hatebreed instead, and a melee follows
years.p: At the New England Metal and Hardcore Festival, sound problems moved Hatebreed onto Anal Cunt's stage. Per Anal Cunt's Josh Martin, Jamey Jasta mocked the crowd, then yelled at Seth Putnam.
years.xp:
Wikipedia's account, sourced to Martin, says the crowd was waiting for Anal Cunt and Jasta told them Hatebreed sold more records. Putnam and his wife were arrested that night.

Hatebreed's side of the story is not in the sources checked.

years.h: Rigg Ross leaves mid-album; Matt Byrne finishes Perseverance
years.p: Hatebreed started recording in November 2000. Ross left in June 2001, and Byrne, still the band's drummer a quarter century later, took over the sessions.

years.src: Wikipedia: Perseverance (Hatebreed album) · Songfacts · Louder (Metal Hammer)
yt: I Will Be Heard live at Hellfest, 2002
years.h: Perseverance arrives on Universal
years.p: Recorded at Long View Farm in Massachusetts with Matt Hyde, it debuts at No. 50 on the Billboard 200 and passes 250,000 units by 2022, per Wikipedia.
years.xp:
Jamey Jasta told Metal Hammer the band made the hardest record it could, to answer the sellout talk: "if people didn't respect how hard we'd worked to get to that point, they weren't ever a fan for the right reasons anyway."

He wrote I Will Be Heard on an acoustic guitar his father gave him, and told Songfacts he knew it would change Hatebreed's career. Lou Richards didn't approve of the song; Jasta went with his gut.

years.big: "I had to become the host of Headbanger's Ball to get my fucking video played!"
years.src: Louder: Hatebreed enlisted · Songfacts · Wikipedia: Hatebreed
yt: Hatebreed: I Will Be Heard (official video)
years.h: MTV won't play Marc Webb's I Will Be Heard video
years.p: Webb, later director of The Amazing Spider-Man, shot it; MTV refused it. The song still landed on the soundtrack to the Vin Diesel film xXx.
years.xp: Jasta told Metal Hammer in 2025 the band's first reaction was "Oh, man, we just wasted a lot of money for nothing!" His fix was to infiltrate the system. He also said that had MTV not eventually played a Hatebreed video, he doubts he'd have gotten the Headbangers Ball job.

eras.title: Jasta gets the MTV2 chair
eras.text: By 2003 Hatebreed was one of the biggest-selling heavy bands in America and its singer was on MTV2 every week. The breakdowns went to Hollywood soundtracks and, in 2005, to the Grammys.

years.h: Jasta beats Killswitch Engage's Howard Jones for the Headbangers Ball job
years.p: He hosted MTV2's show from 2003 to 2007 and used the airtime for [[Terror|697eba1a-bf52-46b1-a19f-4d7190b63e5c]], [[Napalm Death|ce7bba8b-026b-4aa6-bddb-f98ed6d595e4]], [[Madball|c9e0a0f5-9f53-4247-a52d-a3f29d975e17]] and the Hatebreed video MTV had banned.
years.xp: Jasta told Metal Hammer the 'Ball opened the door for Lamb of God, Avenged Sevenfold, Atreyu and As I Lay Dying, while he could still play Terror, Napalm Death, Madball and Decapitated for nine weeks in a row.

years.h: The Rise of Brutality sells 32,515 copies in week one
years.p: Per Wikipedia, the third album debuts at No. 30 on the Billboard 200. Hatebreed songs turn up in Freddy vs. Jason and Saw around the same time.

years.h: Grammy nod for Live for This, then a loss to Motörhead
years.p: Nominated in December 2004 for Best Metal Performance at the 47th Grammy Awards, the song lost to [[Motörhead|57961a97-3796-4bf7-9f02-a985a8979ae9]].

eras.title: Hatebreed goes to Roadrunner and loses a friend
eras.text: Hatebreed moved to Roadrunner and kept charting while its singer's side projects ran on alcohol. In 2006 the guitarist from its first two albums died, and by 2009 Jasta was sober and a founder was back in the band.

years.h: Supremacy opens Hatebreed's Roadrunner years at No. 31
years.p: The fourth album sells 27,000 first-week units, then Hatebreed headlines the Monsters of Mayhem tour with [[Napalm Death|ce7bba8b-026b-4aa6-bddb-f98ed6d595e4]] and Exodus.

years.h: Ex-[[Integrity|f626335d-d234-408d-a67c-37a3c2c7e98a]] and Ringworm guitarist Frank Novinec joins Hatebreed
years.p: Novinec had joined Integrity after Systems Overload and also played in Cleveland's Ringworm and [[Terror|697eba1a-bf52-46b1-a19f-4d7190b63e5c]]. He debuts on Supremacy and outlasts every other Hatebreed guitarist since.

years.h: Lou Richards, who played on two Hatebreed albums, dies at 35
years.p: Richards, who played on Satisfaction Is the Death of Desire and Perseverance and left Hatebreed in 2002, died by suicide, according to Wikipedia.
years.xp: Richards was in Hatebreed from 1996 to 2002. Jamey Jasta has credited him with helping craft the band's metalcore sound, and noted to Songfacts that Richards died a month before turning 36.

years.h: Jasta stops drinking after "too many forgotten nights"
years.p: He told Metal Hammer he quit in 2008 rather than waste the chances he'd been given. That April, Hatebreed signed with Koch Records.
years.xp:
His side projects had been party bands. Kingdom of Sorrow, his sludge band with [[Crowbar|04fc15f9-2555-4699-9215-2ee6c84a2346]]'s Kirk Windstein, started on a 2005 UK tour with Crowbar and, by Jasta's account, was recorded wasted. Icepick, running since 1996, put out Violent Epiphany in 2006.

Jasta also remembers one run with Crowbar and Kingdom of Sorrow for wrecked hotel rooms, a smashed bus window and a bus driver who got hit.

years.h: Sean Martin goes to the studio; founder Wayne Lozinak comes back
years.p: Martin exits on February 9 to work on studio projects, and Lozinak, gone since 1996, returns on guitar.

years.h: After a covers album and a No. 1 DVD, a self-titled record at No. 37
years.p: For the Lions came in May with covers of [[Metallica|65f4f0c5-ef9e-490c-aee3-909e7ae6b2ab]], [[D.R.I.|95f6e954-8bed-4f8e-a53e-d155bb6f7ace]], [[Crowbar|04fc15f9-2555-4699-9215-2ee6c84a2346]] and [[Cro-Mags|9ffa627f-32c2-4cb1-bfad-00cf348abc70]], and the Live Dominance DVD hit No. 1 on Billboard's DVD chart in September.

eras.title: A fan's ashes on the stage
eras.text: Twenty years in, Hatebreed hit its chart peak with a steady line-up of Jasta, Beattie, Byrne, Novinec and Lozinak. Jasta built a second career as a podcaster and producer, and the band's past kept surfacing in odd places, from a UFC octagon to a Cleveland stage.

years.h: The Divinity of Purpose takes Hatebreed to No. 20
years.p: The sixth album of originals also goes to No. 1 on the US Hard Rock chart. The cover is by Eliran Kantor.

years.h: At UFC 158 in Montreal, Chris Camozzi tapes over his Hatebreed logos
years.p: The fighter, a longtime Hatebreed sponsor, said the UFC required black tape across the band's logos on his shirt and banner.

years.h: The Concrete Confessional debuts at No. 25
years.p: The seventh album also charts high in Belgium, Austria and Switzerland, and the band tours it around the world through 2017.

years.h: A dead fan's ashes land on a Cleveland stage
years.p: Dennis Guyot's wish was to be spread there. Hatebreed did it, and later wrote As Diehard as They Come in his honor.

eras.title: Thirty years, one lawsuit
eras.text: Hatebreed hit thirty with sold-out anniversary tours and a new album on the way. It also fired its last founder besides Jasta, and the fight went to court in Connecticut.

years.h: COVID pushes Weight of the False Self from May to November
years.p: Blabbermouth's Dom Lawson called the eighth album the band's strongest in over a decade.

years.h: Thirty years in, Hatebreed plays a matinee at the Toyota Oakdale Theatre
years.p: The 30th anniversary run opened at the Wallingford, Connecticut venue with 100 Demons and [[Shadows Fall|2e3b75d8-00a8-486a-b4e7-a1f8f65e64c9]], then went to Europe with [[Crowbar|04fc15f9-2555-4699-9215-2ee6c84a2346]] and across the US with Carcass.

years.h: Chris Beattie is out, after thirty years
years.p: Beattie, in Hatebreed since 1994, was separated from the band. In a 2025 interview he said it was not his decision, and that someone saw a chance to get him out.
years.xp:
Matt Bachand of [[Shadows Fall|2e3b75d8-00a8-486a-b4e7-a1f8f65e64c9]] took over bass on tour. Matt Byrne told Blabbermouth he couldn't say much because lawyers were involved.

In 2025 Beattie sued Jamey Jasta, citing a 2015 merchandise agreement; Hatebreed calls him a disgruntled former member of an at-will band. In late May 2026 a Connecticut judge let claims including breach of contract go forward, Lambgoat reported, with a possible jury trial in spring 2027.

years.h: Wayne Lozinak steps off a European tour with a brain tumor
years.p: Surgery in August 2025 went well, and he was back by October for the Killswitch Engage UK and Ireland tour.

years.h: Hatebreed signs with BLKIIBLK and announces Fatal Paradox
years.p: The album is set for November 6, 2026, with the single Kill Count Increase. The first new song in five years, Make the Demons Obey, came out in July 2025.
